record.paper_title: A short tour of operator learning theory: Convergence rates, statistical limits, and open questions
record.original_question: Is empirical risk minimization minimax-optimal, in the sense of the noiseless sampling-width formulation, for operator classes beyond holomorphic ones? Examples singled out by the paper include infinitely Fréchet-differentiable operator classes and classes generated by specific parametric PDE problems.

evidence.quote: Moreover, is ERM optimal in the minimax sense of (8) for target classes beyond holomorphic operators? Other sets of interest could include C∞ operators or those arising from specific parametric PDE problems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be (real or complex) separable Banach spaces and let $K \subset X$ be a compact subset (for example, the unit ball of a compactly embedded subspace). Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a class of continuous operators $F : K \to Y$. Given $n \in \mathbb{N}$ "sampling points" $x_1,\dots,x_n \in K$ chosen by the learner (adaptively or non-adaptively), the learner observes the noiseless data $\{(x_i, F(x_i))\}_{i=1}^n$ and produces an estimator $\widehat{F}_n : K \to Y$. Define the sampling (worst-case) width
$$ s_n(\mathcal{F}) \;=\; \inf_{\widehat{F}_n}\; \sup_{F\in\mathcal{F}}\; \sup_{x\in K}\, \|F(x)-\widehat{F}_n(x)\|_Y, $$
where the infimum runs over all measurable reconstruction maps based on $n$ point evaluations. An algorithm is called minimax-optimal in this noiseless sampling-width formulation if the rate of its worst-case error over $\mathcal{F}$ matches $s_n(\mathcal{F})$ as $n\to\infty$ up to constants (or up to logarithmic factors).

Empirical risk minimization (ERM) refers to estimators of the form
$$ \widehat{F}_n \;\in\; \arg\min_{G\in\mathcal{H}_n}\; \sum_{i=1}^n \|G(x_i)-F(x_i)\|_Y^2, $$
where $\{\mathcal{H}_n\}$ is a suitable sequence of hypothesis classes (e.g., neural-network or polynomial surrogate model classes) chosen to approximate $\mathcal{F}$.

It is known that for certain classes of holomorphic operators on infinite-dimensional Banach spaces, ERM-based reconstructions achieve the minimax sampling-width rate. The question is:

Determine whether ERM is minimax-optimal, in the sense of the sampling width $s_n(\mathcal{F})$ above, for operator classes $\mathcal{F}$ beyond holomorphic ones. In particular, settle this for:

(i) classes of infinitely Fréchet-differentiable ($C^\infty$) operators $F : K \to Y$ with prescribed bounds on all Fréchet derivatives;

(ii) classes of solution operators arising from specific parametric PDE problems, namely operators $F$ mapping a coefficient/parameter $a \in K$ to the solution $u(a) \in Y$ of a parametric elliptic, parabolic, or hyperbolic PDE under standard well-posedness assumptions.

In each case, identify the minimax sampling-width rate and prove matching upper bounds achieved (or not achieved) by ERM with an appropriate hypothesis class $\mathcal{H}_n$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as an explicit open question in the operator learning theory literature concerning the minimax optimality of ERM beyond holomorphic operator classes. No published resolution for general $C^\infty$ operator classes or for general parametric-PDE solution operator classes was found; results currently exist for specific holomorphic and (Gevrey/analytic) parametric-PDE settings, leaving the broader question open.

status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly listed as an open problem in operator learning theory.
